observations: Photo 0 and 1 show the same electric milling and grinding machine from slightly different angles.
The machine has a green electric motor at the bottom, connected via a belt to a central shaft with gears.
Above the motor is a blue metal frame supporting a conical metal hopper (funnel) for feeding material.
The hopper is marked with handwritten text, possibly 'Machin' or similar, but not fully legible.
The machine is mounted on a wooden platform with metal legs.
There are visible signs of use: dust, minor rust, and wear on the metal parts.
No power cord or switch is visible in the photos.
The machine appears to be a small-scale, possibly homemade or locally assembled, electric grinder/mill.
